reviewer.identity: general-purpose sub-agent, spawned for 3C-D9; read-only; instructed not to read repositories/cca-conformance

scope: FIPS 180-4 correctness and robustness of Sha256Stream (memoryos-history-admission.js) and sha256Hex (mip-canonical.js): constants derived from prime roots, padding at 55/56/63/64 bytes and above 2^32 bits, schedule and functions, 32-bit arithmetic, chunking and views, invalid inputs, reuse, mutation, performance at 32 MiB; compared with node:crypto on lengths 0-300, random chunking, 1 MiB and 32 MiB.

findings.summary: Sha256Stream.update does not validate its argument and changes length before it can throw: a string, Array or ArrayBuffer corrupts the stream, and a non-Uint8Array typed array is accepted with a wrong digest. The class is not exported and its only caller passes Uint8Array from utf8Encode, so the defect is latent.
findings.note: No production change in this task (candidate is frozen). Recorded as a latent hardening item for the next candidate; no reachable input triggers it.

findings.summary: sha256Hex accepts strings (UTF-8, lone surrogates rejected with INVALID_UNICODE), ArrayBuffer, typed-array views and DataView, and rejects other types; the two implementations differ in input handling.
findings.note: Reviewer states this is correct behaviour, not a defect.

findings.summary: Both are linear; 32 MiB takes about 1.06 s (sha256Hex, 2x memory for a padded copy) and 2.06 s (stream).
findings.note: Not a defect; consistent with the linear-admission requirement (A4.5).

findings.summary: Sha256Stream.hex() works on a clone; update after hex() and repeated hex() are correct.
